c2-gen-0027: On the fourth day God set lights in the firmament, for days and years. Read Genesis 1:14.
c2-gen-0028: Genesis names the first river from Eden. Later Adam named the cattle, the birds, and the beasts. Read Genesis 2:11 and Genesis 2:20.
c3-gen-0018: God divided the light from the darkness. Later Adam called his wife Eve. Read Genesis 1:4 and Genesis 3:20.
c3-isa-0017: Isaiah speaks of His hearing them, and of the blessed of the LORD. Read Isaiah 65:23 and Isaiah 65:24.
c3-gen-0019: The man said the woman gave him of the tree. Earlier, he had spoken of her. Read Genesis 2:23 and Genesis 3:12.
c3-gen-0020: God set the lights in the firmament. Later the heavens and the earth were finished. Read Genesis 1:17 and Genesis 2:1.
c3-gen-0021: God spoke to the woman of sorrow and conception. Earlier, God created man. Read Genesis 1:27 and Genesis 3:16.
c3-gen-0022: The man spoke after he ate. Earlier a man is joined to his wife. Read Genesis 2:24 and Genesis 3:12.
c3-rev-0006: They shall bring the glory and the honor of the nations into the city. John meets one who talked with him there. Read Revelation 21:15 and Revelation 21:26.
c3-rev-0007: Nothing that defiles shall enter the city. Then John sees the throne of God and of the Lamb. Read Revelation 21:27 and Revelation 22:3.
c2-mrk-0010: After John was held under guard, Jesus came to Galilee preaching, and He called people to repent. Read Mark 1:15.
c2-dan-0009: The king has been given a kingdom, power, strength, and glory. Daniel tells what the king saw. Read Daniel 2:31 and Daniel 2:37.
c3-dan-0007: They will tell the interpretation before the king. The toes were partly of iron and partly of clay. Read Daniel 2:36 and Daniel 2:42.
c3-psa-0014: The psalm says His works shall be told to another. It also says the LORD is great. Read Psalm 145:3 and Psalm 145:4.
c3-mat-0012: Great multitudes were gathered to Him. He sat, and the multitude stood on the shore. Read Matthew 13:2 and Matthew 13:10.
c3-dan-0008: The psalm says, “I will extol You, my God, O King;” In Daniel the metals are broken in pieces. Read Daniel 2:45 and Psalm 145:1.
c3-dan-0009: Jesus came to Galilee after John was held under guard. God gave the beasts and birds into the king’s hand. Read Daniel 2:38 and Mark 1:14.
c3-mat-0013: Daniel speaks of a fourth kingdom that will crush the others. Jesus also told a story about the kingdom of heaven. Read Matthew 13:47 and Daniel 2:40.
c3-psa-0015: Daniel speaks of another kingdom inferior to the first. The psalm praises an everlasting kingdom. Read Psalm 145:13 and Daniel 2:39.
c3-mat-0014: The psalm speaks praise to the LORD. Jesus spoke all these things to the multitude. Read Matthew 13:34 and Psalm 145:21.
c2-ezk-0014: The LORD promises to take His people from among the nations, and to bring them into their own land. Read Ezekiel 36:24.
c2-jhn-0022: Jesus speaks of righteousness, because He goes to the Father. He still has many things to say to them. Read John 16:10 and John 16:12.
c3-jhn-0011: Jesus says He tells them the truth as He speaks of going away. Read John 16:7 and John 16:9.
c3-act-0007: This is what was spoken by Joel. The Day of Pentecost had fully come. Read Acts 2:1 and Acts 2:16.
c3-rom-0015: Paul speaks of hoping for what we do not see, and of being saved in this hope. Read Romans 8:24 and Romans 8:25.
c3-jhn-0012: The Father will send One to be with them. Jesus says that One will glorify Him. Read John 14:16 and John 16:14.
c3-act-0008: Peter says, “This Jesus God has raised up, of which we are all witnesses.” The people marveled at those who were speaking. Read Acts 2:7 and Acts 2:32.
c3-act-0009: They had favor with all the people. Peter speaks of the One God raised up. Read Acts 2:24 and Acts 2:47.
c3-rom-0016: Paul says the creation was subjected to futility. He also speaks of those who are in the flesh. Read Romans 8:8 and Romans 8:20.
c3-gal-0003: Paul warns, “Let us not become conceited,” and he also speaks of these two. Read Galatians 5:17 and Galatians 5:26.
c2-deu-0016: The LORD promised to raise up one like Moses from among their brethren. Read Deuteronomy 18:18.
c2-exo-0023: The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron while they were in Egypt, and He spoke about this month. Read Exodus 12:1 and Exodus 12:2.
c3-lev-0005: The verse describes what Aaron shall put on his body. Then he comes before the LORD at the door of the tabernacle. Read Leviticus 16:4 and Leviticus 16:7.
c3-exo-0008: The verse names when they shall keep it. A neighbor is included as they count the animal. Read Exodus 12:4 and Exodus 12:6.
c3-heb-0010: The priests always went into the first part of the tabernacle. The first covenant also has ordinances of divine service. Read Hebrews 9:1 and Hebrews 9:6.
c3-lev-0006: That day is a sabbath of solemn rest, and Aaron brings the live goat after his work in the Holy Place. Read Leviticus 16:20 and Leviticus 16:31.
c3-lev-0007: The priest who is anointed shall sprinkle some of the blood of the bull on the mercy seat. Read Leviticus 16:14 and Leviticus 16:32.
c3-gen-0023: The LORD says, “By Myself I have sworn,” As they reached the place, Abraham stretched out his hand. Read Genesis 22:10 and Genesis 22:16.
c3-heb-0011: The high priest went in alone once a year, not without blood. The verse also names the Holiest of All. Read Hebrews 9:3 and Hebrews 9:7.
c3-heb-0012: Hebrews mentions foods and drinks and various washings. It also speaks of the ark and the mercy seat. Read Hebrews 9:5 and Hebrews 9:10.
c2-psa-0024: The psalm describes those who see the speaker and ridicule Him. They also shoot out the lip. Read Psalm 22:7.
c2-isa-0025: Isaiah asks, “Who has believed our report?” Read Isaiah 53:1 and Isaiah 53:4.
c3-psa-0016: The psalm asks that God not be far, for trouble is near. It opens with a cry to God. Read Psalm 22:1 and Psalm 22:11.
c3-isa-0018: My righteous Servant shall justify many. Isaiah also says He was cut off. Read Isaiah 53:8 and Isaiah 53:11.
c3-jhn-0013: They filled a sponge with sour wine and put it to His mouth. They also took His garments and made four parts. Read John 19:23 and John 19:29.
c3-psa-0017: John quotes another Scripture, and the psalm says the wicked have enclosed Him. Read Psalm 22:16 and John 19:37.
c3-jhn-0014: The LORD has laid on Him the iniquity of us all. The soldiers came and saw that He was already dead. Read John 19:33 and Isaiah 53:6.
c3-psa-0018: The Servant shall justify many. The psalm also calls the speaker a reproach of men. Read Psalm 22:6 and Isaiah 53:11.
c3-mic-0009: The psalm says, “Our fathers trusted in You;” Micah speaks of this One, and then of the Assyrian. Read Micah 5:5 and Psalm 22:4.
c3-mat-0015: Isaiah asks, “Who has believed our report?” Herod gathered the chief priests and scribes. Read Matthew 2:4 and Isaiah 53:1.
c2-isa-0026: Isaiah says the glory of the LORD has come upon His people. Read Isaiah 60:1.
c2-isa-0027: Isaiah speaks of the foreigner who has joined himself to the LORD, and of a gift in His house and within His walls. Read Isaiah 56:3 and Isaiah 56:5.
c3-isa-0020: The LORD speaks of the fast He has chosen. Read Isaiah 58:6 and Isaiah 58:9.
c3-isa-0021: The LORD says, “Here I am, here I am,” to a nation that had not sought Him. Read Isaiah 65:1 and Isaiah 65:5.
c3-isa-0022: My servants shall sing for joy of heart. Then the LORD speaks of the earth. Read Isaiah 65:14 and Isaiah 66:1.
c3-isa-0023: The LORD says, “Keep justice, and do righteousness,” He also speaks of light dawning in the darkness. Read Isaiah 56:1 and Isaiah 58:10.
c3-isa-0024: Isaiah speaks of the eunuchs who keep His Sabbaths. Violence is no longer heard in the land. Read Isaiah 56:4 and Isaiah 60:18.
c3-isa-0025: You shall delight yourself in the LORD. He will look on him who is poor and of a contrite spirit. Read Isaiah 58:14 and Isaiah 66:2.
c3-isa-0026: Isaiah speaks of what remains before the LORD, and then he speaks of the gates. Read Isaiah 60:11 and Isaiah 66:22.
c3-isa-0027: Isaiah says, “Before she was in labor, she gave birth;” He also speaks of Sharon. Read Isaiah 65:10 and Isaiah 66:7.
c2-ezk-0015: Ezekiel is taken to the gateway and sees a man. Read Ezekiel 40:3.
c2-ezk-0016: He is told to look, hear, and fix his mind on everything shown him. The verse names the dates, and then the hand of the LORD came upon him. Read Ezekiel 40:1 and Ezekiel 40:4.
c3-ezk-0009: The verse says, “This is the law of the temple:” They may be ashamed of their iniquities. Read Ezekiel 43:10 and Ezekiel 43:12.
c3-ezk-0010: They shall put on linen garments in the inner court. He is brought back to the outer gateway of the sanctuary that faces east. Read Ezekiel 44:1 and Ezekiel 44:17.
c3-ezk-0011: They shall inherit the land with one another. The city is also measured on the north side. Read Ezekiel 47:14 and Ezekiel 48:30.
c3-ezk-0012: He was set on a high mountain. If the people are ashamed, he is to make the temple known to them. Read Ezekiel 40:2 and Ezekiel 43:11.
c3-ezk-0013: He heard Him speaking from the temple. The priests are to wear linen turbans and linen trousers. Read Ezekiel 43:6 and Ezekiel 44:18.
c3-ezk-0014: A district is set apart, twenty-five thousand cubits in width. The priests shall teach the people the difference between the holy and the unholy. Read Ezekiel 44:23 and Ezekiel 48:8.
c3-ezk-0015: They shall divide this land among themselves according to the tribes of Israel. Then the verse gives the distance all the way around. Read Ezekiel 47:21 and Ezekiel 48:35.
c3-ezk-0016: He was brought toward the east. Later he describes the three northward openings of the city. Read Ezekiel 43:1 and Ezekiel 48:31.
